title: Video‐Based Rainfall Opportunistic Sensing in Hydrology: A Lightweight Machine Learning Approach
content:
Abstract

Video-based rainfall measurement is a frontier topic in opportunistic sensing; however, rapid, accurate, and robust identification of rainfall-related rain-streak features from dynamic videos remains a key challenge, especially for monitoring devices with limited computational resources. To address the trade-off between measurement accuracy and efficiency, we propose a lightweight machine-learning approach termed the Coupled Image Enhancement and Gradual Aggregation Network (CIEGA-NET). Inspired by image deraining in autonomous driving, CIEGA-NET reconstructs background information through image enhancement and then extracts clean rain-streak signals by image differencing. It also uses a coarse-to-fine temporal aggregation strategy to learn continuous features from rainfall videos, avoiding superpixel processing and optical-flow alignment. Tests on public synthetic data sets and 23 real rainfall events from Shenzhen, Hangzhou, and Dalian, using surveillance cameras and smartphones under day and night conditions and a wide range of rainfall intensities, show that CIEGA-NET estimates event rainfall with a mean relative error of 8.2%. Compared with existing video-based methods, it reduces errors by nearly 10% overall and by up to 25% in heavy rainfall. Moreover, CIEGA-NET achieves a processing speed of 26 frames per second at commonly used resolutions, which is two orders of magnitude faster than CNN-based methods and one order of magnitude faster than physics-based methods. These results indicate that the lightweight architecture of CIEGA-NET enables efficient rainfall measurement and may provide a promising, low-cost solution for future high-density rainfall monitoring networks.
